miniProject.title: Continuous-batching scheduler with collapse and recovery evidence
miniProject.brief: Build a deterministic continuous-batching simulator in `sim/` with budgets, preemption, priorities, cancellation and overload handling, and test it against public scheduler cases and frozen adversarial corpora. Carry one bounded policy into a real engine behind a flag and defend the win and the loss from traces.
steps: Build the `sim/` continuous-batching simulator with token and sequence budgets, decode-first fill and deterministic replay, and check it against the TensorTonic continuous-batching scheduler cases plus your hand trace as the first regression test.

Add KV-reserve admission with recompute preemption to `sim/`, counting preemptions per request, and assert ownership, no-overcommit, progress and bounded-wait invariants after every transition over randomized histories with a seeded leak and a stuck waiter they must catch.

Run the Module 05 chunk-budget sweep in `sim/` with decode-first fill, and keep the throughput table with inter-token latency tails that shows where a smaller budget steadies the stream and where it starves the hardware.

Add priority classes with an aging rule to `sim/`, prove a convoy workload delays short requests under arrival order, keep a starvation test that fails with aging off, and pass the TensorTonic cache-aware routing cases for the affinity policy.

Implement abort at every scheduler phase with leak checks, early rejection with retry budgets, and goodput over offered load; then sweep open-loop load through saturation with repeats, keeping raw records, drain time and the queueing against execution split.

Freeze long-prefill, decode-heavy, mixed, bursty, priority and cancellation corpora, compare two policies from per-request traces keeping one regression, then carry one bounded change into a real engine behind a flag with fallback and run the companion continuous-batching pair.
deliverables: The `sim/` scheduler with replayable traces, invariant checks and the hand-trace regression test.
Adversarial corpora with per-policy traces, saturation sweeps with drain evidence and the ablation with its losing regime.
The bounded engine change behind a flag with fallback, cancel and routing tests and the scheduling write-up.

checks.name: TensorTonic: Simulate Continuous Decode Batching
checks.note: Pass the public scheduler cases in your harness; reconcile reserve rules with your simulator.

checks.name: TensorTonic: Route Cache-Aware Prefill Requests
checks.note: Pass the public routing cases; use the ranking as the affinity policy oracle.

checks.name: AI Systems Performance Engineering continuous-batching pair
checks.note: Run the baseline against optimized comparison on your hardware; keep one losing workload.

rubric.pass: Fixed corpus, config and ordering replay to identical per-request traces, and the hand trace matches exactly.
rubric.strong: A second policy replays cleanly, and trace diffs attribute every delay to a named scheduler decision.

rubric.pass: Admit, defer and preempt decisions match budget math on fixed mixes, and per-request preemption counts explain eviction churn.
rubric.strong: A repeated-eviction workload shows the reserve fix that stops the churn with traces before and after.

rubric.pass: Cancel-at-every-phase tests leak no blocks, rejection protects goodput, and sweeps show the knee with drain time.
rubric.strong: The queueing against execution split names the saturated bottleneck, and the ablation keeps a losing regime.

rubric.pass: The starvation test fails with aging off and passes with it on, and the bounded engine change toggles to fallback cleanly.
rubric.strong: Routing cases pass, and engine traces explain where the simulator prediction held and where it broke.

miniProject.feedsInto: The simulator, corpora, sweeps and bounded change feed the kernels dispatch, distributed routing, production overload handling and the capstone contribution.
